title: The Selfish Giant
author: Oscar Wilde; adapted for Shellfie
credit: A short adaptation of the garden episode from Oscar Wilde’s The Selfish Giant (1888), Project Gutenberg #902. The original ending, including its religious imagery, is omitted.

pages: Every afternoon after school, children played in a beautiful garden. Soft grass covered the ground, peach trees stretched their branches, and birds sang above the games. The garden belonged to a Giant, but he had been away for a long time. The children loved the peaceful place and wished they could play there every day. When school was over, they hurried to meet one another beneath the trees.

When the Giant returned, he was surprised to find children in his garden. “This garden is mine,” he told them, and he sent them away. Then he built a high wall around the garden so no one could enter. Outside the wall, the children missed the flowers, the soft grass, and the shade of the trees. They talked about the games they had played together there after school.

Spring arrived in the rest of the countryside. Birds returned, and blossoms opened on the trees. But inside the Giant’s garden, winter stayed. Snow covered the grass, frost touched the branches, and a cold wind blew. The Giant sat by his window, puzzled. He wondered why spring had forgotten his garden. Beyond the wall, the warmer days had returned, but his own trees remained bare.

One morning the Giant heard a bird singing. He looked outside and saw children sitting in the trees. They had found a little opening in the wall. Wherever they played, the branches were covered in blossoms. In one corner, though, a small child stood beside a tree, unable to reach its branches. Snow still lay on the ground there. The child walked around the tree, looking for a way up into its branches.

The Giant saw the child and felt sorry for keeping everyone out. He went outside and gently lifted the child into the tree. At once the tree blossomed, and birds began to sing. The other children had run away when the Giant appeared, but now they saw his kindness and came back. As the children returned, spring filled the rest of the garden too.

The Giant opened the garden to the children and took down the wall. That afternoon he played with them among the flowers and trees. He had thought the garden would make him happy if he kept it all for himself. Now he discovered how much joy came from sharing it. The children had a place to play, and the Giant had new friends.

quiz.q: What did the Giant build around the garden?
quiz.ev: Then he built a high wall around the garden so no one could enter.

quiz.q: Why did the children return after the Giant came outside?
o: They saw him help the small child
He offered them a new wall
They wanted to hide from spring
